The disagreement stems entirely from tool errors (API failures and parsing failures) when two models attempted to audit the patch file, not from actual security concerns.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is caused by tool errors, not security findings. qwen3-235b encountered an HTTP 400 error when auditing dxvk-extraopts.patch, and openrouter/free failed to parse a decision from the model response for the same file. deepseek-v4-flash successfully audited all files and marked them safe. This is a tool reliability issue, not a genuine security disagreement.

learnings: Implement automatic retry logic for transient API errors (HTTP 400, 500, timeouts) before marking a file as inconclusive
Add fallback parsing strategies when models don't follow the expected XML/JSON format for security decisions
Distinguish between 'inconclusive due to tool error' and 'inconclusive due to genuine uncertainty' in the verdict logic - tool errors should trigger retries, not escalate to human review
When multiple models fail on the same file, investigate whether the file format or content is causing systematic parsing issues
